title: Candace Owens' Anomalies
dek: Candace Owens says the Charlie Kirk case doesn't add up. We put every piece of her evidence next to the court record. Here's what held up and what didn't.
body: On September 10, 2025, Charlie Kirk was shot and killed while speaking to students at Utah Valley University in Orem. Within days Candace Owens, his former Turning Point USA colleague and now one of the biggest podcasters on the right, started pointing at 'anomalies.' A year later she has floated Israel, Egypt, France, a time machine and her late friend's own widow. Her audience has only grown: Media Matters, a liberal watchdog, counts more than 24.5 million followers across her platforms.
So let's do what she says she's doing: look at the evidence. Hers, point by point, and the court's.
## What the court has

Tyler Robinson, 22, surrendered the night after the shooting after a family member tipped off a friend who called the sheriff. Prosecutors charged him with aggravated murder and six other counts and say they'll seek death.

The evidence laid out in charging papers and a weeklong July preliminary hearing: DNA consistent with Robinson's on the rifle's trigger, a fired casing and the towel the rifle was wrapped in. Surveillance video of him on campus and on the rooftop. His parents recognizing him in FBI photos, and his father saying the rifle matched one given to Robinson as a gift. Texts and a note to his roommate, a recording in which Robinson says he wished he hadn't done it, and a Discord post before he surrendered.

On September 1, 2026, Judge Tony Graf sent the case to trial on all seven counts and kept the death penalty on the table. Robinson pleaded not guilty. His lawyers have attacked the DNA as possible transfer but offered no other suspect. No trial date yet; the next hearing is October 23.
> There is one shot. There is one bullet. There is one victim. (Defense attorney Staci Visser)
## Her evidence, and how it held up
= The Egyptian plane | Debunked

Her evidence: crowdsourced flight-tracking showing an Egyptian Air Force jet leaving Provo at 13:08, which she read as just after the shooting, proof of 'a military operation.' How it holds up: 13:08 was UTC. In Utah that's about 7 a.m., hours before the shooting. Owens posted that she 'stand[s] corrected' but still called it abnormal.
= Egyptian planes tracking Erika Kirk | Unproven

Her evidence: an on-screen spreadsheet of supposed location 'overlaps' between military planes and Erika Kirk over three years, credited to a 'pregnant mommy sleuth.' How it holds up: no news outlet has verified the spreadsheet. Erika Kirk's reply: if you want to go through my flight log, go right ahead.
= Israel did it | Unproven

Her evidence: Kirk's leaked private texts complaining about losing a Jewish donor, an account of a tense Hamptons meeting with investor Bill Ackman, and the planes. How it holds up: Turning Point confirmed the texts were real, but they show frustration, not threats. Ackman denied any 'intervention' and posted a friendly exchange with Kirk afterward. FBI Director Kash Patel says there's no credible information tying any foreign government to the killing. In an August debate, the Washington Times reported, Owens conceded she had no direct proof.
= Trained by the French Foreign Legion | Debunked

Her evidence: an unnamed French government source and a screenshot of a joint U.S.-French military exercise in California. How it holds up: France's armed forces ministry said Robinson was never in the Legion and could not have been trained by it.
= Robinson was never on campus | Debunked

Her evidence: an hourlong video drawing inferences, with a former Utah politician at the center. How it holds up: video played in court shows Robinson moving around campus before the shooting. Gov. Spencer Cox told people not to believe it.
= 'The Feds made up the texts' | Unproven

Her evidence: unnamed 'leaks' and the observation that the messages lacked timestamps. She repeatedly called them Discord messages; they were texts from Robinson's phone. How it holds up: the texts came in alongside DNA, video and a recorded admission, and a judge found probable cause on every count. Nobody, including Robinson's own lawyers, has shown evidence of fabrication.
= The roommate was 'never questioned' | Debunked
How it holds up: recordings of the FBI questioning him were played at the preliminary hearing.
= The bullet didn't match the rifle | Disputed

Her evidence: a defense filing saying the ATF couldn't identify an autopsy bullet fragment to the rifle. How it holds up: this is the one real wrinkle, and it's real. But PolitiFact found the result was 'inconclusive,' not a mismatch, and experts say that's common with fragmented rifle bullets. The ATF reportedly did match the casing to the rifle, and the FBI is running a second test.
> Unable to identify is not the same as ruled out. (Jason Pack, retired FBI agent)
= The exploding microphone | Debunked

Her evidence: slowed-down footage, a montage of Kirk's microphones, photos of 'shards' and a test video of an explosive. How it holds up: the medical examiner certified a gunshot wound to the neck, police recovered a rifle, casing and bullet fragments, and there was no sign of explosive residue or shrapnel.
= Inside job at Turning Point | Unproven

Her evidence: by her own account to Piers Morgan, no concrete evidence against the two staffers she pointed at. Slate reported she has also cited a dream and Erika Kirk's demeanor at the funeral. How it holds up: Patel's answer on any Turning Point role was one word, 'Zero.' Turning Point sent her cease-and-desist letters.
= Kirk the 'time traveler' | Unproven
Her evidence: private texts she says she has, and her memories of conversations. How it holds up: she hasn't published them. Slate found no kernel of truth.
## It's in court now

Two people she linked to the case are suing her for defamation. Kirk's former security chief, Brian Harpole, sued in Nashville in April after she aired a claim he was at a classified Army meeting the day before; his suit says travel records put him in Dallas. Owens argues her statements are opinion and questions, and that motion is pending. In September, a Utah man she suggested looked more like the stairwell figure than Robinson sued in federal court; his suit says video puts him in the crowd at the time. Separately, French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife are suing her in Delaware over different claims.
> Stop. That's it. That's all I have to say. Stop. (Erika Kirk)

The fight has split the right. Ben Shapiro said she's been 'vomiting' conspiracy nonsense for years. Sen. Mike Lee called her take on the case insane. Others like Tucker Carlson mocked efforts to deplatform her. Owens calls her critics 'Zionist PR.'
## The Report's verdict

Asking questions is a journalist's job. The job also includes checking the answers. Of the claims we tracked, the plane, the Legion, the campus and the roommate collapsed under basic checking, and the biggest ones, Israel, Turning Point and the widow, have nothing behind them but tips, dreams and spreadsheets nobody can verify. The only genuine open question, the bullet fragment, is exactly the kind of thing a trial is for.

Robinson is presumed innocent until a jury says otherwise. If the state's case has holes, his lawyers will find them in court, under oath, with evidence both sides can test. That's where this belongs.
